newsitem.title: USA: Mexico rebounding from recession, Rubin says.
newsitem.headline: Mexico rebounding from recession, Rubin says.

text.p: Mexico's economy steadily rebounded during the third quarter from a steep recession last year as it met all payment obligations under a U.S. aid pact, Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin told Congress on Friday.

"The Mexican economy is rebounding from the deep recession of 1995," Rubin told lawmakers in a regular monthly report detaling progress since a U.S. financial bailout package was made available to Mexico in February 1995.
"Second-quaretr 1996 GDP grew 7.2 percent compared to a year earlier, and recent economic indicators point to continued growth in the third quarter," Rubin said.

The monetary and fiscal policies pursued by Mexico "continue to be solid," Rubin said. The Mexican government has imposed a stringent austerity program to get its finances in order and, in mid-October, announced another "modest tightening" of monetary policy, Rubin noted.

A restructuring of Mexico's hard-pressed banking system still is under way. A Spanish bank took a 75 percent interest in Grupo Financiero Invermexico late in October, marking the fourth recent purchase of a Mexican bank by a foreign investor, Rubin said.
The Clinton administration agreed last year to make up to $20 billion available to help Mexico recover from an economic crisis, though not all of the money was drawn.
"Mexico has met all payment obligations to date under the U.S. financial support program," Rubin said.
Including a $7 billion prepayment in August, Mexico has repaid a net $9 billion in outstanding swaps representing nearly three-quarters of its U.S. debt, Rubin said. It still owes $3.5 billion.
Mexico announced in mid-October that it was scaling back its plans for petrochemical privatization, Rubin noted, but agreed to "fully open" new petrochemical investments to private investors.
